sources.entry: rarfile - A RAR archive reader with a zipfile-like API.

summary.one_liner: rarfile is a Python module for reading RAR archives (RAR3 and RAR5) with an API modeled on the standard zipfile module.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Python module for opening and reading RAR archives with an interface that follows zipfile. It supports RAR3 and RAR5 formats, multi-volume archives, Unicode filenames, and password-protected archives, and it can read archive and file comments. Archive parsing and non-compressed files are handled in pure Python. Compressed content is extracted by calling an external tool, with unrar preferred and unar, 7zip, bsdtar, or unrar-free as alternatives. The README lists per-backend limitations, such as bsdtar not supporting multi-volume or password-protected archives.
use_cases: Listing the contents of a RAR archive from Python
Extracting files from RAR archives in a script
Reading files from password-protected RAR archives
Reading RAR comments and filenames in Unicode
notable: Mirrors the zipfile API, so code written for zip archives can be adapted to RAR
Pure Python parsing of RAR headers; external tools are needed only to decompress compressed data
Several interchangeable extraction backends with a documented feature matrix
Supports both RAR3 and RAR5 archives, including multi-volume sets
caveats: Compressed files require an external tool (unrar, unar, 7zip, bsdtar, or unrar-free) to be installed
Backend support varies: bsdtar lacks multi-volume, solid, and password-protected archive support; unar lacks RAR2 locked files and RAR5 Blake2 checking
On MacOS, the README recommends MacPorts rather than Homebrew for installing unrar or 7zip
